findings.rule: 284-c10 / D68 ('N credits added' from the ledger delta, else the truthful toast); Constitution I.1
findings.trigger: Prod. held = snapshot(uid-1, balance 1). The user taps Restore. The before read stores 1. restorePurchases posts an owned token and the server credits 5. The after refreshConfirmed starts (generation 5) and its fetch is in flight. A second refresh then starts (generation 6), for example from PurchaseRestorer handling an unsolicited purchase (restorePurchases -> recorded -> scope.launch { credits.refresh() }), from AppViewModel.refreshWallet, or from a TailoringRunner record(). The after fetch returns 6, but started (5) != generation (6), so the snapshot is discarded. The function still returns held.value?.owner == owner, which is true because the stale snapshot 1 is held. 'after' reads 1, the delta is 0, and the user is told 'No previous purchases found' while 5 credits were just restored. The hero jumps to 6 when the newer refresh lands. 'Confirmed' means 'some snapshot for this owner is held', not 'my fetch was stored'. The same applies to the before read. Also, no core:data test pins refreshConfirmed's return value (OfflineFirstCreditsRepositoryRemoteTest has none). The VM tests use the RemoteStyleCreditsRepository fake, so if the prod override always returned true, the round-1 medium would come back without failing a test. Fix: return true only when this call stored its snapshot (move the result into the started == generation && owner == remote.owner() branch, false otherwise, which gives the truthful 'Couldn't check purchases' toast). Then add one repository test.
findings.title: refreshConfirmed reports a superseded fetch as confirmed, and its real return value is untested
findings.proof: OfflineFirstCreditsRepositoryRemoteTest, with a remote that has two fetch gates. Seed held at 1 with refresh(). Launch refreshConfirmed() A with gate 1 open and the snapshot set to 6. Launch refresh() B with gate 2. Release A and assert A returns false, or assert observeBalance().first() == 6 whenever it returns true. Today it returns true with balance 1. Add a second case: remote.failure = IOException makes refreshConfirmed() return false.
